prompt: Put the steps of one TDD cycle in order.
items: write the least code that passes
tidy the code with the tests green

prompt: A new test passes the first time it is run, before any code is written for it. What does that say?

choices.text: TDD is working perfectly, and the next step is to refactor the code
choices.why: Green before red skips the step that proves the test can fail.
Right: a test must be seen failing before the code exists.

prompt: In TDD, the step where the code is tidied without changing what it does, with the tests kept green, is called ___.
Why is a test written after the code weaker than one written before?
hint: Has it ever been seen failing?

choices.text: It has never been seen failing
choices.why: Right: a test that cannot fail looks exactly like a test that passes.

choices.text: It runs more slowly than a test that was written first

prompt: Why does TDD not replace testing?

choices.text: Unit tests are not allowed to run in continuous integration pipelines
choices.why: They run there all the time.

choices.text: Its tests cover only the examples somebody thought of
choices.why: Right: a case nobody thinks of gets no test, and the suite is green.

choices.text: TDD tests are slower than manual tests

prompt: The first run shows ERROR rather than FAIL. What is the difference?
hint: Could the test run at all?

choices.text: ERROR: it could not run; FAIL: it ran and got the wrong answer
choices.why: Right: here, coupons.py did not exist.

choices.text: ERROR is worse for the student

prompt: Rafael’s first coupons.py returns 3100 whatever it is given. Why is that a reasonable step in TDD?

choices.why: It is wrong as a feature and right as a step.
She pointed out what it gets wrong.

choices.text: It is the least code that passes, and it exposes what is untested
choices.why: Right: the next example has to make the fake fail.

prompt: In the test, prices are in centavos. How many centavos does an order of R$ 36,00 with PIPOCA cost?

hint: Read it from the inside out.

choices.why: It compares the result of the call.

choices.text: That PIPOCA is a valid Python name in the coupons file

choices.why: Only on the way to the comparison.

choices.text: That apply returns 3100 for PIPOCA and 3600

hint: Two examples pulling in different directions.

choices.text: Adding examples until a fake cannot pass them all
choices.why: Right: the code is forced to stop guessing.

prompt: The failure says AssertionError: 3100 != 3600. Which number did the code return?

choices.why: That is what the test expected.
The first one is the result.
Right: the fake gave five reais off to XYZ.

prompt: Why does the third test use 2800 rather than 3600?

choices.text: Lowercase codes only work at matinées, according to Joana’s rule
To check the discount comes off the total it was given
choices.why: Right: not from a number the code happens to remember.

prompt: On this TDD team, where did the examples in the second and third tests come from?

choices.why: Right: Rafael wrote the code and tests, the cases came from the conversation.
He wrote them down; he did not think of them alone.

choices.text: Célia’s defect report about pasted codes with spaces

prompt: Which of these are the tester’s contribution on a TDD team, by this lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: rerunning by hand what the unit tests prove
Writing a new test for each line moved
choices.why: Nothing new is promised, so nothing new is tested.
Right: and only as wide as the examples.
A refactor does not change behaviour.

prompt: If no test covered lowercase codes, what could the refactor have done unnoticed?
hint: The safety is only as wide as the examples.

choices.text: Changed the price of every matinée ticket at the box office

choices.why: Right: every remaining test would still pass.

prompt: Célia reports that " PIPOCA " with spaces gave no discount. What does Rafael do first?

choices.text: Writes a test that fails on it
choices.why: Right: a defect is reproduced as a failing test before it is fixed.

choices.text: Adds .strip() to the code and ships the fix the same afternoon
choices.why: Then nothing proves the fix, or keeps it.

choices.text: Asks Célia to stop pasting codes and type them by hand instead
choices.why: The box office is how the product is used.

choices.text: Closes the report as a user error
choices.why: Joana’s rule says the code is the code.

prompt: Four tests are green. Which questions do they leave unanswered, by this lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.why: No: the third test covers it.

prompt: A green TDD suite is described in this lesson as a record of what?

choices.why: Right: not proof that the right ones were.

choices.text: Every defect the code can have
The hours the developer worked on the feature this sprint
